rubric.required_finding: Distinguishes40:1 totalPBMC:tumor from1:1 enrichedVδ1:tumor and rejects an intrinsic potency comparison.
Uses83%αβ and8.6%Vδ1 to explain mixed-effector contribution and rejects exclusiveVδ1 attribution.
Recognizes seven-day priming/activation history as a confounder rather than interchangeable exposure.
Preserves only context-specific observations and does not invent normalized potency/lysis percentages.
Proposes matched purifiedVδ1 input/activation and selective depletion/add-back or lineage controls with causal interpretation.

reference_answer: The comparisons do not establish greater intrinsic potency perVδ1 cell in the PBMC preparation. The40:1 ratio uses total PBMCs as its denominator, whereas the skin-cell assay uses an enriched Vδ1 effector preparation at1:1. In the reported PBMC mixture, only8.6% of cells are Vδ1 and83% are αβT cells; changing the total-cell ratio therefore changes both potential Vδ1 input and the number of other cells. The seven-day priming history also changes activation state and composition, so it cannot be treated as interchangeable with the skin-derived-cell assay. All PBMC-mediated lysis cannot be assigned exclusively toVδ1 cells from an aggregate mixed-cell readout. αβT cells, accessory-cell interactions and priming-dependent changes remain alternative or contributing explanations. The corrected conclusion is that the source demonstrates activity in two distinct effector contexts, without a matched estimate of perVδ1-cell potency or exclusive causal attribution. A first discriminating experiment is to compare purified Vδ1 cells from both preparations at matched viable Vδ1:tumor ratios and matched activation histories. A second is selective Vδ1 depletion and add-back in the PBMC mixture, paired with αβT-cell or accessory-cell controls and live target-cell counts. These tests separate cell-intrinsic activity from mixture and priming effects.

all_no.text: Every project claim is false. None of the supplied measurements supports any assay-specific conclusion.
